notes: This heading organises references; it is not an additional physical menu.
Issue 25 page 16 describes RIGHT for entry but page 19 also calls RIGHT normal/off. ON/OFF are deliberate neutral labels; physical direction is not asserted.

Mode +10 and Select +1 enter numeric codes. The exact initial display, wrap and alphabetic-bank entry sequence are not established. Code 00 is an explicit fictional starting point; Choose code is a labelled training assist.

Enter sets/reviews a source-backed option. The checked source does not explicitly say a second Enter unsets it. Restore training configuration is a separate fictional reset and preserves other local records.
The source marks codes 21,22,71–78,81–88,A1–A8 and E1–E8 as not complying with EN54-2.
Three buzzer pips every few seconds indicate level3. Exact cadence is not claimed. Zone-test reset is after a few seconds; non-latching reset can take up to 20 seconds when sounders operate.
Opening or refitting the simulated door does not operate Write Enable. Leave the switch OFF after practice; the source says General Fault remains lit if it is left ON.

numbering.explanation: These are documented physical controls, indications and engineering functions. They are not LCD menu screens. Displayed configuration codes retain the manual’s exact spelling. Configuration codes such as 00 and 2A are preserved as strings; they are not route addresses.

examples.meaning: Documented sounder-delay choice, 30 seconds; not an access PIN.
Version-limited configuration reference; no supported simulation effect.

caveats: Mode +10 and Select +1 enter numeric codes. The exact initial display, wrap and alphabetic-bank entry sequence are not established. Code 00 is an explicit fictional starting point; Choose code is a labelled training assist.

Enter sets/reviews a source-backed option. The checked source does not explicitly say a second Enter unsets it. Restore training configuration is a separate fictional reset and preserves other local records.
Issue 25 page 16 describes RIGHT for entry but page 19 also calls RIGHT normal/off. ON/OFF are deliberate neutral labels; physical direction is not asserted.

navigation.action: Provides the documented operator access; distinct from internal Write Enable.
Select ON to reach level 3 in the trainer; source switch direction conflict remains visible.

coverage.strategy: Derived from FINDR’s existing reviewed manufacturer sources; references, supported simulation and authored practice tasks remain distinct.
mappedAreas: Documented physical keys, indications and internal controls.
Source-backed operator functions and all existing guided lessons.
All 103 configuration-code records, preserving 48 supported and 55 reference-only effects.
excludedAreas: A fictional eight-zone K11080M2 K-series fixture with common alarm operation. It is not a T-series wiring or CP-A AlarmSense simulator.

This conventional panel identifies circuits by zone, not individual addressed detectors. Disablement affects the whole selected zone. Adding or replacing a detector is circuit work followed by checks and testing; there is no detector enrolment menu.
Active-device warning on a disabled zone is scoped to sigma_CP 214.hex or later, as stated by the main manual. It is not assumed for older panels.

The operator manuals do not establish the complete MODE cycle order. An explicit training target chooser avoids inventing a hardware press count. Engineering start, wrap and alphabetic code-entry details are also not fully documented.
Page 16 says move Write Enable to the right for access level 3, while page 19 calls the normal/off position right. The trainer uses ON/OFF labels and does not assert a switch direction.

The manual describes Enter setting an engineering option and a flashing dot showing that it is set; it does not explicitly describe unsetting it with a second press. Restore training configuration is a separate simulation action, not a hardware button sequence.

Test auto-reset is described only as after a few seconds. Non-latching zones may take up to 20 seconds to reset when sounders operate. Advancing the training clock or test cycle does not certify a measured hardware timer.

Removing or refitting the simulated cover does not change Write Enable or erase settings. The cover-off illustration shows the source panel plate and switch aperture, not an invented view of the full cabinet, power supply or batteries.

Only supported configuration effects are simulated. T-series/zonal sounder, ancillary-board, intrinsically safe barrier, short-circuit threshold and unverified version-specific options remain reference-only. No live electrical work, detector compatibility decision or real repair is certified.

The source user guide has an Issue 06 cover and _05 page footers. The newer Issue 25 main manual is primary; saved/downloaded Sigma records are not hash-pinned by the archive and their edition must be checked.
